sources_read.section: the hook to guard and consume

scope: Guard usePresence against missing ids; a presence-rail container showing the peer count and the leader indicator; mounting it in the document view; tests. Out of scope: painting peer cursors on the canvas (needs the page's displayed geometry), and publishing cursors (needs a pointer stream).

acceptance_criteria.text: With no sessionId/profileId, usePresence opens no channel and returns empty peers.
The rail shows 'Only you' with no peers, 'N here' with peers, and the leader badge while the leader draws; the leader id comes from the members meta.
The document composition renders the rail; no store hook under src/app (I4) and no feature->feature import (I3).

open_questions: The leader's profileId is read from the members meta (META.members), the roster's own home; duplicating it would drift. features/presence may not import features/workspace's MemberMeta type (I3), so it reads the two fields it needs.
Q8 (unanswered: the real tablet mix) and D-11 (defaulted: device parity) leave the rail's mobile placement to 022.
Peer-cursor canvas painting and cursor publishing are deliberately out of scope; they need the page's displayed size/rotation and a pointer stream, and are a separate task.
risks: Opening a live channel before a session is known would subscribe to live: with an empty id; the guard closes that.
A second leader source would drift; the rail reads the roster meta only.
The rail mounts app-level (I4-safe) and consumes the shared context, so it adds no feature coupling.
